title: KAP: Bridging the Knowledge Selection-Runtime Consumption Gap in LLM Systems
event_hint: KAP paradigm introduction: Knowledge Access Planning for LLM serving with GraphSpec implementation
problem: The Knowledge Selection-Runtime Consumption (KSRC) gap: LLM serving backends receive only serialized prompts, losing structured knowledge priors (ranked evidence, graph topology, multimodal alignment, confidence signals) from upstream selection processes. This forces uniform full-context KV consumption regardless of actual knowledge importance, increasing latency and degrading throughput as contexts lengthen.
mechanism: Knowledge Access Planning (KAP) elevates structured knowledge priors to first-class execution artifacts through a universal intermediate representation (runtime access plan). The IR encodes selected knowledge units, runtime object mappings, logical positions, access policy, and verification policy. Instantiated as GraphSpec with Graph-RAG frontend and VLLM backend, using compiler-executor architecture to translate structured priors into KV access plans without altering model weights, training, or logical prompt semantics.

evidence.claim: GraphSpec reduces proposal-time KV access to 5.5% of source KV state at 128K context length while maintaining answer quality comparable to full-context decoding
evidence.condition: 128K-token long-context QA workload, proposal-time KV access metric

evidence.claim: GraphSpec achieves 1.19x decode-throughput speedup at 128K context length versus full-context decoding
KAP decouples physical KV consumption from prompt length, fundamentally shifting long-context generation scaling trajectory
evidence.baseline: linear physical cost growth with context length

evidence.claim: GraphSpec instantiation connects Graph-RAG knowledge-selection frontend to VLLM LLM serving backend

evaluation_context: Long-context QA workloads spanning 4K to 128K token contexts. Knowledge-selection frontend uses Graph-RAG to produce structured priors (graph topology, ranked evidence). LLM serving backend uses VLLM. Evaluation metrics include proposal-time KV access percentage, decode throughput speedup, and answer quality comparison to full-context decoding baseline. No hardware platform, latency absolute values, or deployment scale visible in evidence pack.
limitations: Evaluation limited to long-context QA workloads; generalization to other task types (code generation, multi-turn dialogue, agentic workflows) not addressed in visible evidence. Verification/fallback overhead not quantified. Phase-boundary model presented but positive-speedup regime conditions not fully specified in abstract/introduction. GraphSpec is one concrete instantiation; KAP paradigm generality claimed but only Graph-RAG+VLLM combination demonstrated.
project_relevance: Directly addresses AI infra horizontal dynamics question: which systems/hardware changes affect end-to-end efficiency. KAP introduces execution-time planning layer between knowledge selection and LLM serving, potentially reducing GPU memory bandwidth pressure and improving throughput for RAG systems. Relevant to serving-runtime optimization direction. However, missing production deployment data and hardware-specific benchmarking limit immediate actionability. Should be tracked as infra-level optimization paradigm; may warrant dedicated topic if adoption emerges in production serving stacks.

evidence_gaps.question: What are the absolute latency reductions (ms), GPU memory savings, and end-to-end query completion times? Throughput speedup (1.19x) is visible but baseline latency not provided.
What hardware platform (GPU model, memory bandwidth, interconnect) was used for evaluation and at what batch size/concurrency?
